fields.statement: Verified at eb5352e6. Read the diff (internal/api/session_run.go blockedNotice.echoes/notify in followRex; internal/api/run.go rexNoticeMsg split out of rexNotice). Ran go test ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(session-run-blocked-notice|run-blocked)$' -count=1: both PASS, and the new script passed 3 more runs in a row. The script runs session run under a fake rex whose events give the agent's blocked report, the echo of the wrapper's report, then working. It checks exactly one root-record state=blocked:kind=permission:app=rhiza report whose title is the tab and whose msg names the change set, the build step, the tab and the question, and no state=working. session show gives the agent's blocked report while blocked and working after. Also checked: kind=question in a non-autonomous run, no report for an autonomous question, a report for an autonomous permission block. Mutation checks in scratch copies: dropping the echo skip fails the script at line 36 (the record takes the echoed message), and dropping the autonomous-question filter fails it at line 64. The driver writing no report rests on code this commit does not change (cmd/rhiza/ctx.go sets ctx.Rex only when REX_BLOCK is set). The script drives session run with --run directly, not a full headless run driver. go vet, fmt-check and self-check OK. go test ./... -timeout 40m: all cmd/rhiza scripts pass. Only the timing tests internal/api TestReadBudget and internal/slice TestBudget fail, at load average about 16-23 from concurrent agents; the diff touches neither read path. A default make check hit the 10m package timeout because plan-workflow takes about 400s here, and the parent commit 46cc1d58 is just as slow (431s).
